# UInt 〔BlitzLLVM〕

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [BlitzBasic](BlitzBasic) · [Math](BlitzBasic-Math)

```blitzbasic
UInt:Int32 value:Float32
```

**〔BlitzLLVM〕** This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

<!-- AUTOGENERATED COPYRIGHT HEADER START -->
Converts a number or a text to a UInt, a 32-bit integer from 0 to 4294967295. This is a BlitzLLVM extension: the originals only know `Int` and `Float`. A whole number below 0 or above the limit keeps its lowest 32 bits (`UInt(-1)` is 4294967295), a real is rounded to the nearest whole number (halves go to the even one) and stops at 0 or 4294967295 if it is outside. Use [SatUInt](SatUInt) to stop whole numbers at the limits as well. `Int` converts back, which makes 4294967295 a -1 again.

```blitzbasic
Print UInt(-1)
Print UInt(5000000000.0)
Print Int(UInt(-1))
```

```text
4294967295
4294967295
-1
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | Float32 | required | A number or a text with a number in it. |

**Returns:** The UInt.

**Differences and known gaps:**

* Not in the originals, which have no integers of other sizes.
